A throwaway Muneral was built from this head on arcana-devs (own PostgreSQL 16 cluster on loopback port 55531 inside runs/A2-255, one-off credentials, API on 127.0.0.1:3531, no privileged command, nothing on a production host) and read over HTTP before and after the change. Receipts, command by command, are in /home/dev/aup/arc2/runs/A2-255/evidence/: baseline-bind.txt (the pre-change bind on every interface, answering on the mesh address), after-default-bind.txt, after-container-bind.txt, probe-default.txt, probe-as-gate.txt, contract-test-vs-old-probe.txt (the new probe contract test run against the PRE-change probe script: 9 of 12 cases red, including the A2-251 sentinel hole), drift-guard-red.txt (each arm of the deployment contract test red under its own mutant), api-test-run.txt. The exemptions were attached by this card, the admitting agent, and not by the verifier or the gate; no verdict in this receipt was edited.

[a2255-broker-hole] /health can only name a commit the build was given one. On arcana-prd the deploy runs through arcanada-compose-broker, which exports BUILD_SHA only for services listed in its BUILDSHA table — Arcanada-one/model-connector deploy/arcanada-compose-broker.sh:234, and as of 2026-09-24 that table lists transcribator-api only. This change therefore lands a mechanism that reports `build.sha: null` WITH a reason in production until a one-line change to that root broker (a separate repository, a deploy script, and out of this card's scope) registers muneral. Recorded as a hole rather than presented as a working commit identity: reverse_if the follow-up card is dropped, because an endpoint that permanently answers not_measured is worse than none.
